evidence_items.publisher: Chengshuai Zhao and colleagues, Arizona State University; arXiv
evidence_items.explanation: The controlled synthetic experiments support the proposed distribution-shift mechanism within their tested setting. They do not identify the claimed development efforts, establish their targets, or show why those targets were missed.

evidence_items.publisher: Rem Yang and colleagues, MIT and Brown University; arXiv
evidence_items.explanation: Tests across ten models found improved generalization on code-reasoning tasks, including mutated and generated programs intended to probe distribution differences. This limits a blanket inference of generalization failure, but success on these tasks does not establish adequate broad generalization or resolve the claimed cause of missed development targets.

evidence_items.publisher: Parshin Shojaee and colleagues, Apple; arXiv
evidence_items.explanation: The study establishes failures on controlled puzzle tasks as complexity increases. It does not isolate training-distribution mismatch as their cause or connect them to the development efforts Marcus describes.

unresolved_gaps: No identified set of the claimed development efforts with documented capability targets and measured shortfalls.
No located evidence directly linking those shortfalls to distribution shift across the claimed efforts.
The controlled studies test particular tasks; extending their results to broad frontier-model development requires additional evidence.
Commercial models' training exposure is not established by the cited code-reasoning comparisons, limiting certainty about the precise distribution shift.
